errors.title: TypeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute
errors.cause: A variable you expected to hold an object is `None`, and you called a method/attribute on it. Common with functions that return None on failure paths, dict.get() defaults, or API calls that returned nothing.
errors.fix: Before accessing, check the value: `if obj is not None:`. Then trace WHY it is None - find the function that produced it and check its failure/early-return paths.

errors.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named
errors.cause: Python cannot find the module: it is not installed in the current environment, or you are running with a different interpreter/venv than the one where it is installed.
errors.fix: In the SAME shell run `which python` (or `where python` on Windows) to confirm the interpreter, then `python -m pip install <module>`. If using a venv, activate it first. For local packages check the folder is on sys.path.

errors.title: ImportError: cannot import name (circular import)
errors.cause: Most often a circular import: module A imports B while B (directly or transitively) imports A back, so one of them is only half-initialized when the import runs.
errors.fix: Move the offending import inside the function that uses it (lazy import), or restructure so the shared code lives in a third module both can import.

errors.title: KeyError
errors.cause: You accessed a dict key that does not exist in that dictionary.
errors.fix: Use `d.get(key, default)` when absence is normal, or check `if key in d:`. If the key SHOULD exist, print the dict (or its keys) right before the failing line - usually an upstream typo or a different data shape than expected.

errors.title: IndexError: list index out of range
errors.cause: You indexed a list past its end - typically an empty list (index 0 of []) or an off-by-one loop bound.
errors.fix: Check `len(lst)` before indexing, or iterate with `for item in lst` instead of by index. An empty list usually means the upstream query/parse returned nothing.

errors.title: AttributeError: object has no attribute
errors.cause: The object's real type does not have that attribute - usually because the variable holds a different type than you assume (e.g. a module shadowed by a local variable, a str where you expected an object, or a partial import).
errors.fix: Print `type(obj)` right before the failing line. Watch out for a local file/folder named the same as an imported module - that shadows it.

errors.title: IndentationError / TabError
errors.cause: Mixed tabs and spaces, or inconsistent indentation levels. Python treats indentation as syntax.
errors.fix: Configure your editor to insert spaces (PEP 8: 4 spaces) and convert existing tabs. In vim: `:set expandtab ts=4 retab`. In VS Code the bottom-right indicator switches Tab Size / Spaces.

errors.title: RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
errors.cause: A function calls itself without a reachable base case - or two functions call each other in an infinite mutual recursion.
errors.fix: Identify the recursive function and add/verify the base case that stops recursion. If recursion depth is legitimately large, raise the limit with `sys.setrecursionlimit()` or rewrite iteratively.

errors.title: ValueError: could not convert string to (int|float)
errors.cause: You called int()/float() on a string that is not a clean number - usually user input, a CSV cell with spaces/quotes, or an empty string.
errors.fix: Strip first: `float(s.strip())` and handle empties: `if not s: ...`. For user-facing input wrap in try/except and show a friendly message.

errors.title: ZeroDivisionError
errors.cause: A division or modulo by zero - a denominator computed as 0, often from an empty aggregate (sum of nothing, count of zero).
errors.fix: Guard the denominator: `if n: avg = total / n else: ...`. Find where the zero comes from before papering over it.

errors.title: PermissionError: [Errno 13]
errors.cause: The OS denied file/directory access: wrong owner, read-only path, or you are writing where you lack permission (e.g. / or /usr on Linux).
errors.fix: Check `ls -l` ownership of the target. Run as the right user (avoid blanket sudo), or write to a path your user owns. On Windows check the file is not open in another program.

errors.title: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2]
errors.cause: The file or directory path does not exist at the location Python looked for it - almost always a relative-path vs working-directory mismatch.
errors.fix: Use absolute paths or anchor to the script: `Path(__file__).parent / 'data.json'`. Print `os.getcwd()` to see where the process actually runs.

errors.title: BrokenPipeError / ConnectionResetError
errors.cause: The other end of the socket closed before/while you wrote or read. Common when a client aborts a download or a server restarts.
errors.fix: Catch the exception around socket writes and treat as client-gone. For servers, log and continue - this is normally not a bug in your code.

errors.title: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode
errors.cause: You are decoding bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (GBK/Latin-1 files, Windows-1252 exports, or binary data opened as text).
errors.fix: Open with the real encoding: `open(f, encoding='gbk')` / `latin-1`, or detect it (chardet). For binary files open in 'rb' mode.

errors.title: pip: externally-managed-environment
errors.cause: Newer distros (Debian 12+, Ubuntu 23.04+) protect the system Python; pip refuses to install into it.
errors.fix: Create a venv: `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install ...`, or use `pipx` for CLI tools, or add `--break-system-packages` only if you really know.

errors.title: SSLError: certificate verify failed
errors.cause: Python cannot verify the server's TLS chain: missing system CA store, corporate proxy MITM, outdated certifi, or a self-signed cert.
errors.fix: First fix the cause: update certifi (`pip install -U certifi`), check system time. Corporate proxy: export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to the proxy CA. As a LAST resort only, verify=False (never in production).

errors.title: Flask: Working outside of application context
errors.cause: You used something that needs the Flask app (current_app, db, request) outside a request/setup - typically in a script, a background thread, or module import time.
errors.fix: In scripts/CLI wrap code with `with app.app_context():`. In threads pass needed values in as arguments instead of touching request.

errors.title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined
errors.cause: You accessed `.something` on undefined/null - the object was never set, the async data has not arrived yet, or a typo in the property chain.
errors.fix: Optional-chain defensively: `obj?.a?.b`, and find where the object should have been created. For async data, render only after it arrives (loading state / guards).

errors.title: TypeError: X is not a function
errors.cause: The name you called is not a function on that object: wrong import shape (default vs named), a variable shadowing the function, or the method does not exist in that runtime/version.
errors.fix: console.log the object itself. Check import syntax: `import x from` vs `import { x } from`. For browser APIs check compatibility (some exist only in newer runtimes).

errors.title: SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON
errors.pattern: Unexpected token ('?<|u)'?.*in JSON|Unexpected end of JSON input
errors.cause: `<` means the server returned HTML (an error page, a login redirect, a 404) but you called response.json(). The API did not answer with JSON.
errors.fix: Log `await response.text()` before parsing to see what actually came back. Check the request URL, method, auth headers, and the server's error/redirect behavior. Then parse conditionally based on content-type.

errors.title: blocked by CORS policy
errors.pattern: blocked by CORS policy|Cross-Origin Request Blocked
errors.cause: The browser blocked a cross-origin fetch because the server did not send permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers for your origin. This is enforced client-side; it is a SERVER configuration issue.
errors.fix: On the API server add CORS headers for your origin (e.g. flask-cors, cors npm package) - allowing credentials requires an explicit origin, not `*`. A proxy through your own backend also sidesteps it.

errors.title: Node: EADDRINUSE: address already in use
errors.cause: Another process is already listening on that port - usually a previous instance of your app that did not exit.
errors.fix: Find it: `lsof -i :3000` (mac/linux) or `netstat -ano | findstr :3000` (Windows), kill the stale PID. Or run the new instance on another port.

errors.title: ECONNREFUSED
errors.cause: Nothing is listening on the host:port you tried to connect to - the target service is down, the host/port is wrong, or a container/localhost network boundary is in the way.
errors.fix: Verify the service is running and on that port (`curl host:port`). Inside Docker compose use the service name, not localhost. Check firewall/security-group rules.

errors.title: npm ERR! ERESOLVE / peer dependency conflict
errors.cause: Two packages demand incompatible versions of the same peer dependency - common after upgrading React or a major library.
errors.fix: Read the conflict report: either upgrade the conflicting package, or as an escape hatch `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`. Clean state first: delete node_modules + package-lock.json and reinstall.

errors.title: Module not found: Error: Can't resolve
errors.cause: Webpack/Vite cannot resolve an import path: wrong relative path, missing file extension config, or the package is not installed.
errors.fix: Check the exact path and case (case-sensitive on Linux/CI!). `npm install` the missing package. For alias imports (@/...) verify the bundler alias config.

errors.title: TS: Object is possibly 'undefined'
errors.cause: With strictNullChecks, TS proves the value could be null/undefined at that point and forces you to handle it.
errors.fix: Narrow it: `if (x === undefined) return;`, use optional chaining `x?.y`, or provide a default `x ?? fallback`. Do NOT blanket-suppress with `!` unless you truly guarantee it.

errors.title: TS: Property 'X' does not exist on type
errors.pattern: Property '.*' does not exist on type
errors.cause: The declared type does not include that property: wrong type annotation, an untyped/any-shaped API response, or a missing interface field.
errors.fix: Update the interface/type to match reality, or narrow with a type guard. For dynamic API payloads define the response type explicitly instead of casting.

errors.title: React: Each child in a list should have a unique key
errors.cause: React needs a stable identity for list items to reconcile renders efficiently.
errors.fix: Give each element a stable unique key: `items.map(i => <Row key={i.id} />)`. Use the item's natural id - NOT the array index when the list can reorder.

errors.title: React: Maximum update depth exceeded
errors.cause: A setState is being called inside render or inside an effect with unstable dependencies, causing an infinite re-render loop.
errors.fix: Look for setState called unconditionally in useEffect or during render. Fix dependencies or move the update behind a condition/event.

errors.title: Git: fatal: not a git repository
errors.cause: You are in a folder that is not inside a git working tree (or .git was deleted, or you are one directory level off).
errors.fix: `cd` to the project root and `ls -a` to confirm .git exists. If missing entirely, re-init and re-add the remote; if you are in a subfolder, go up.

errors.title: Git: failed to push some refs (remote ahead)
errors.cause: The remote has commits you do not have locally - git refuses to overwrite history.
errors.fix: `git pull --rebase` (or fetch + rebase your branch), resolve any conflicts, then push again. Never `--force` on shared branches.

errors.title: Git/SSH: Permission denied (publickey)
errors.cause: SSH could not authenticate: the key is not loaded, not registered on the host (GitHub/GitLab), or ssh is offering the wrong key.
errors.fix: `ssh -T git@github.com` to test. Generate with `ssh-keygen`, add the public key to your account, ensure the agent has it (`ssh-add`), and confirm the remote uses SSH (git@) not HTTPS.

errors.title: Git: refusing to merge unrelated histories
errors.cause: The two branches have no common ancestor - typical when a repo was initialized twice (e.g. local git init + a remote that got its own README commit).
errors.fix: If you are sure: `git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories`, resolve conflicts, commit. Otherwise reset to the correct history first.

errors.title: Git: detached HEAD state
errors.cause: HEAD points at a commit instead of a branch - fine for looking around, but new commits will be orphaned.
errors.fix: To keep working: `git switch -c new-branch` from here; to go back: `git switch main`.

errors.title: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon
errors.pattern: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon|docker daemon is not running
errors.cause: The Docker daemon is not running, or your user cannot reach /var/run/docker.sock.
errors.fix: Start it: `sudo systemctl start docker` (or start Docker Desktop). If permission errors, add your user to the docker group and re-login.

errors.title: Docker: port is already allocated
errors.cause: Another container or host process already binds that port.
errors.fix: `docker ps` to find the container using it; stop it or map a different host port (-p 8081:80). On the host, lsof/netstat shows non-docker squatters.

errors.title: no space left on device
errors.cause: Disk full - commonly Docker build cache/images/volumes have eaten the disk.
errors.fix: `docker system df` to see usage; reclaim with `docker system prune -a --volumes` (careful: removes unused images/volumes). Check host disk with `df -h`.

errors.title: MySQL: Access denied for user
errors.pattern: Access denied for user.*(?:MySQL|@)|Access denied for user
errors.cause: Credentials or host grant are wrong: bad password, the user is not allowed to connect from that host, or the client connects to the wrong server.
errors.fix: Verify with `mysql -u user -p -h host` using the same creds the app uses. Check the user's host pattern in `SELECT host,user FROM mysql.user;` - 'localhost' grants do not cover TCP from other machines.

errors.title: MySQL: Unknown column / table doesn't exist
errors.cause: The schema does not match the query: missing migration, wrong database, or a typo in the identifier.
errors.fix: Run `SHOW TABLES;` / `DESCRIBE table;` on the exact DB the app connects to. Pending migrations: run them (alembic/django migrate). Case sensitivity matters on Linux.

errors.title: PostgreSQL: password authentication failed
errors.pattern: password authentication failed for user|no pg_hba\.conf entry
errors.cause: pg_hba.conf does not allow this user/host/method combination, or the password is wrong.
errors.fix: Check pg_hba.conf rules match your connection (host/user/db/method), reload postgres (`SELECT pg_reload_conf();`), and reset the password via the superuser if needed.

errors.title: 502 Bad Gateway (nginx upstream)
errors.cause: nginx reached for your backend but it is down, crashed, or too slow (504).
errors.fix: `systemctl status <app>` and app logs first - this is almost never an nginx problem. Check the upstream port/socket matches, and worker timeouts for 504s.

errors.title: 413 Request Entity Too Large
errors.cause: The request body exceeds the server's size limit (nginx client_max_body_size or framework limit).
errors.fix: Raise the limit where it applies: nginx `client_max_body_size 20m;`, or framework config (e.g. Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH).

errors.title: SSH: HOST KEY VERIFICATION FAILED / remote host identification
errors.pattern: HOST KEY VERIFICATION FAILED|Remote host identification has changed
errors.cause: The server's host key changed (rebuild/re-IP) and your known_hosts still has the old one - or in scripts, ssh never got an answer about trusting the host.
errors.fix: If the change is expected: `ssh-keygen -R host` then reconnect and accept. In CI use `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`.

errors.title: Connection timed out / proxy issues
errors.cause: Packets cannot reach the target: firewall/security group, wrong host, or an env proxy variable (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) hijacking the request.
errors.fix: `curl -v host:port` from the same machine to bisect. Check `env | grep -i proxy` - stale proxy vars break fetches. Verify cloud security-group/firewall rules.

security.title: Hardcoded AWS Access Key
security.why: An AWS access key ID is embedded in source. Anyone with repo access (or a leaked build artifact) gets your cloud account.
security.fix: Revoke it in IAM immediately (hardcoded keys are considered compromised), rotate, and load from environment variables or a secrets manager.

security.title: Private key material in code
security.why: A private key is embedded in the file. This is the crown jewel - treat it as leaked the moment it lands in code or chat.
security.fix: Revoke/rotate the key, generate a new one stored in a secrets manager or key file outside the repo, and add the pattern to .gitignore/secret scanning.

security.title: Hardcoded OpenAI-style API key (sk-...)
security.why: A sk- prefixed API key appears in source; leaked keys get scraped by bots within minutes and can rack up huge bills.
security.fix: Rotate the key at the provider dashboard now, then read it from an environment variable (.env, not committed).

security.title: Hardcoded GitHub token (ghp_/github_pat_)
security.why: A GitHub personal access token is in the code; it grants repo/account access until revoked.
security.fix: Revoke at GitHub Settings > Developer settings, issue a new one via fine-grained tokens, inject via secrets (GitHub Actions secrets / env).

security.title: Hardcoded Slack token (xox...)
security.why: A Slack token is embedded in source and can be used to read/write workspace data.
security.fix: Revoke it in Slack app settings and rotate; load from environment.

security.title: Hardcoded Google API key (AIza...)
security.why: A Google API key is embedded in source; quota theft and billing abuse are common.
security.fix: Rotate in Google Cloud Console, restrict by referrer/API, and inject via environment.

security.title: Generic credential assignment
security.why: A long literal string assigned to a credential-like variable name. Verify it is not a real secret (placeholders like 'changeme' are fine).
security.fix: If real: rotate and move to environment/config outside VCS. If a placeholder, rename it (e.g. PASSWORD_ENV) so scanners stop flagging it.

security.title: eval()/exec() on dynamic input
security.why: eval/exec turn strings into code. If any part of the string is user-influenced, this is arbitrary code execution.
security.fix: Replace with explicit logic (dict dispatch, getattr with allowlist, json.loads for data). If truly unavoidable, validate input against a strict allowlist.

security.title: subprocess with shell=True
security.why: With shell=True the command string goes through the shell; injected metacharacters turn into arbitrary OS commands.
security.fix: Pass an argument list and shell=False (the default). For pipes, use shlex.quote on interpolations or do it in Python instead of the shell.

security.title: os.system() / os.popen() usage
security.why: os.system builds a shell command from a string - classic command injection when any component is dynamic.
security.fix: Use subprocess.run([...], shell=False, check=True) with an argument list.

security.title: SQL built with f-string / concat / format
security.why: SQL text assembled from interpolated values allows SQL injection - the single most exploited web vulnerability class.
security.fix: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("... WHERE id = %s", (val,)). ORMs' bound parameters are safe too. String-formatting into SQL is never acceptable.

security.title: pickle.loads on untrusted data
security.why: Unpickling attacker-controlled bytes executes embedded Python code - deserialization RCE.
security.fix: Use JSON (or another non-executing format) for anything crossing a trust boundary. pickle only for your own local, trusted caches.

security.title: yaml.load without SafeLoader
security.why: yaml.load with the default loader can construct arbitrary Python objects from the YAML - deserialization RCE.
security.fix: Use yaml.safe_load() (or yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)).

security.title: Server-side template built from string
security.why: Rendering user-influenced strings as templates allows SSTI -> full server compromise ({{ }} escape into Python).
security.fix: Render static template files with dynamic values passed as context variables, never build template text from input.

security.title: XML parser without entity protection
security.why: Default Python XML parsers resolve external entities, enabling file-read (XXE) and billion-laughs DoS against attacker-supplied XML.
security.fix: For untrusted XML, defuse entities (defusedxml) or disable DTDs/entity resolution in the parser config.

security.title: JWT verify without algorithm pinning
security.why: Decoding JWTs without an explicit algorithms allowlist enables the 'alg: none' / algorithm-confusion attacks - forged tokens accepted.
security.fix: Always pin: jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=["HS256"]).

security.title: TLS verification disabled (verify=False)
security.why: Certificate validation is off: any network MITM can read/modify the traffic. Usually added to 'fix' an SSL error - that hides the real problem.
security.fix: Fix the trust chain (proper CA bundle, proxy CA). If you must call a self-signed internal service, pin its certificate instead.

security.title: innerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML with dynamic value
security.why: Writing dynamic HTML into the DOM without sanitization enables stored/reflected XSS.
security.fix: Use textContent for plain text. If rich HTML is genuinely required, sanitize server-side with a strict allowlist (DOMPurify / bleach).

security.title: CORS wildcard origin
security.why: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * lets any website read responses - dangerous when credentials/cookies are involved.
security.fix: Set an explicit origin allowlist; with credentials, the exact origin is required by spec anyway.

security.title: Redirect to user-supplied URL
security.why: Redirecting to a URL taken from the request enables phishing that shows your domain.
security.fix: Validate against an allowlist of relative paths or trusted hosts before redirecting (urlsplit + netloc check).

security.title: MD5/SHA1 used (password/token context)
security.why: MD5/SHA1 are broken for security purposes (collisions, fast brute-force). Passwords need slow, salted hashes; integrity needs SHA-256+.
security.fix: Passwords: bcrypt/scrypt/argon2. File/integrity digests: SHA-256. (MD5 is fine only for non-security cache keys.)

security.title: PRNG used for tokens
security.why: Mersenne-Twister PRNG is predictable - tokens, reset links, session ids made from it are guessable.
security.fix: Use the secrets module (Python) or crypto.getRandomValues / crypto.randomBytes (JS/Node).

security.title: Debug mode hardcoded
security.why: Debug mode in production leaks source, stack traces, and (Werkzeug) can expose an interactive console = RCE.
security.fix: Gate by environment: debug only when ENV=dev, off by default. Never expose the Werkzeug debugger publicly.

security.title: Flask SECRET_KEY hardcoded
security.why: The session-signing key is in source; repo access lets attackers forge session cookies.
security.fix: Generate per-deployment (secrets.token_hex(32)) and load from environment.

security.title: World-writable permissions (0o777)
security.why: 0o777 lets any user on the host write/replace the file - privilege escalation foothold.
security.fix: Grant the minimum: 0o644 for files, 0o755 for dirs, owner-limited for secrets.

security.title: Predictable temp file (tempfile.mktemp)
security.why: mktemp returns a name without creating it - race window lets an attacker pre-create/symlink the path.
security.fix: Use tempfile.mkstemp() / NamedTemporaryFile(create=True) which create securely by construction.

security.title: assert() used for access control
security.why: Python strips asserts under -O optimization: your authorization check disappears in production.
security.fix: Use explicit `if not allowed: abort(403)` style checks that run in all modes.
